title: Q2 两级调度：卡车跨区 + 三轮车区内
summary: R2 adds the three conditional items from the T024-R1 acceptance and follows the instruction to change the headline when the cap-60 point moves. (1) Cap 60: the priced optimum becomes 889 tricycles (50 zones, median 18.5, max 44, zero zones at the cap), cell-level unmet 40,041.58 (1.88%), vehicle-km 4,150.99, layer cost 267,530.20, total 591,587.42, saving 927,691.53 (61.06%). The cap sweep is 741/802/865/885/889 at caps 20/25/30/40/60 with 17/7/4/1/0 zones at the cap. (2) Executability: the LP time budget amortises trip distance over a full load, so the priced 889 cannot schedule its own integer trips city-wide - 534 of 13,775 trips (3.9%) go unassigned in 15 zones, and blanket buffers do not fix it (10% leaves 347, 20% leaves 307). A per-zone fixed point (raise the fleet until its own LP trip list is schedulable, then re-solve) closes at 975 tricycles with zero unassigned in all 50 zones. The executable plan has unmet 38,489.44, full-load-equivalent vehicle-km 4,213.04, layer cost 524,279.23, total 608,086.97, saving 911,191.98 (59.98%); with actual-load plus deadhead mileage (9,367.93 km, 1,873.59 CNY) the total is 609,117.95 and the saving is 910,161.00 (59.91%). Executable-basis break-evens: 1.4612 CNY per removed unmet trip, 1,234.56 CNY per tricycle-day. The paper must quote the executable pair (975 / 608,087 / 59.98% on the full-load convention), not the LP-layer 889 / 61.06%. (3) The sample zone 24, now at its priced allocation of 44, runs 395 integer-load trips with zero unassigned and a minimum feasible fleet of 14; penalty rows carry zones_at_nmax (p=10 keeps 3 zones at the cap, so its 1,340 is a lower bound).

checks.2_sample_schedule: pass; evidence=data/runs/T024/schedule_check.json. Zone 24, priced allocation 44, LP solved at n=44: 395 integer trips, all scheduled, unassigned 0, max load 20, last completion 19.29 h, max deadhead 0.280 km, loaded vehicle-km 215.71, bicycle-km 3,461.57 (average load 16.05). LP full-load vehicle-km 173.78, LP bicycle-km 3,475.65 (matches the stored curve at n=44 exactly). Rounding: 2 flows dropped (0.72 bicycle), loss 26.50 of 6,192.50 (0.428%), bound 81.5, sink excess 1. The minimum fleet that executes the same 395 trips under the greedy earliest-finish rule is 14; the 10% buffer case (49 tricycles, same trip list) also has 0 unassigned but is not priced. The R1 mismatch (priced 40, scheduled 44) is gone: the priced allocation is itself 44.
checks.3_city_executability: pass (finding, not pass/fail): at the priced 889, the city-wide integer schedule has 13,775 trips, 534 unassigned (3.88%) in 15 zones; the largest are zone 9 (135 of 3 tricycles), zone 29 (87 of 6), zone 21 (51 of 1). Blanket buffers at 1.05/1.10/1.15/1.20 give 959/1,003/1,045/1,088 tricycles but still leave 357/347/322/307 trips unassigned, so a percentage buffer is not the fix. Cause: the LP time coefficient 2d/(V Q)+2h/60 charges distance time per bicycle as if every trip carried Q bikes; partial-load integer trips cost 2d/V per trip, and the per-hour budget is exceeded. Evidence: schedule_check.json city and buffer_sweep.
checks.4_executable_fixed_point: pass; evidence=schedule_check.json exec_rows/exec_totals. For each zone the fleet is raised until the LP at that fleet produces a trip list its own fleet can schedule; 15 zones were raised, the fixed point closes at 975 tricycles (+9.7%), zero unassigned in all 50 zones. Unmet 38,489.44 (removed 200,755.76). Full-load convention: vehicle-km 4,213.04, mileage 842.61, fixed 292,500, penalty 230,936.62, layer 524,279.23, total 608,086.97, saving 911,191.98 (59.975%). Actual-load+deadhead convention: 9,367.93 km, mileage 1,873.59, layer 525,310.20, total 609,117.95, saving 910,161.00 (59.907%). Difference 1,030.98 CNY/day (0.17% of total). Executable-basis break-evens: penalty ceiling 1.46119 CNY per removed trip; fixed ceiling 1,234.56 CNY per tricycle-day. The fixed point uses the same greedy rule and is therefore an upper bound on the executable fleet; a better scheduler or a re-optimised allocation could lower it, so 608,087 is an upper bound on the executable cost and 59.98% a lower bound on the saving.

notes: Cap 60 changes the optimum from 885 to 889 and removes the last capped zone (0 at cap). The gain is 691.37 CNY/day (0.12%); the R1 numbers are superseded everywhere. The sweep 20/25/30/40/60 is monotone in total cost, so no further cap increase is suggested by the data.

The LP time budget is the root cause of the executability gap: t = 2d/(V Q) + 2h/60 charges the distance time per bicycle as if every trip were full, while the integer schedule charges 2d/V per trip. Partial loads therefore exceed the per-hour budget. The fixed point repairs this by raising the fleet, not by changing the cost model; a proper fix would put the integer trip count into the LP (a MILP or an iterative ceiling), which is out of scope here and is flagged for T021.

The fixed-point fleet 975 is an upper bound: it uses the same greedy earliest-finish rule, and a better assignment or a re-optimised allocation under the executable cost could lower it. Likewise 608,087 is an upper bound on the executable cost and 59.98% a lower bound on the saving.

The 10% blanket buffer arithmetic (974 for the old 885 fleet) is reported but not used: at 1.10 the per-zone buffer is 1,003 tricycles and 347 trips still go unassigned, because the failure is concentrated in a few zones with very small allocations (zone 21 has 1 priced tricycle and 51 unassigned; the fixed point raises it to 4).

The sample zone 24 schedule is the largest allocation and is executable at its priced 44 (min feasible 14). Its LP full-load vehicle-km is 173.78 while the loaded schedule travels 215.71 km plus 40.11 km deadhead; the ratio is the same as the city-wide one, which is why the actual-load mileage cost is 1,873.59 rather than 842.61.

The global threshold 0.4311 CNY per removed trip is an LP-cost-model property (computed over the fleet scan with the LP curves). On the executable plan the threshold is 1.4612 and the fixed-cost ceiling 1,234.56; the paper should quote the latter and may mention 0.4311 only as the idealised bound.

N*(p) at cap 60: 203/457/580/731/889/1,340 for p=1/2/3/4/6/10. p=10 still has 3 zones at the cap, so 1,340 is a lower bound; the other rows are uncapped. Global LP-model threshold is unchanged at N=100 because no low-fleet allocation touches the cap.
